D.treatment: Inductive education with experiential learning early

cells.note: The study predicts improvement in learning outcomes but reports no printed effect size or experimental comparison.

D.treatment: greater surgical experience with increasing case order

result.effect: console time decreased by 33.2 minutes over the first 14 procedures; mean reduction 2.6 minutes per case

cells.quote: The predictive model estimated a substantial reduction in console time with increasing surgical experience. Based on modelled values, console time decreased by 33.2 min over the first 14 procedures (20.5% without lymphadenectomy and 18.4% with lymphadenectomy), with a mean estimated reduction of 2.6 min per case, defining the point of initial deceleration (marginal reduction <1.0 min/case).
cells.note: Case order was modeled as experience; this was an observational learning-curve analysis rather than an assigned intervention.

result.effect: Welch’s F(2, 9.815) = 14.497, p < 0.001; Cluster 1–Cluster 3 mean difference −162.2, 95% CI [−263.20, −61.19]

cells.quote: A one-way Welch ANOVA was conducted to determine whether the three clusters' completion times differed. Completion times significantly differed between the three clusters, Welch’s F (2, 9.815) = 14.497, p < 0.001. Hames-Howell post-hoc analysis revealed that the mean increase from Cluster 1 to Cluster 3 (− 162.2, 95%CI [− 263.20, − 61.19]) was statistically significant.
cells.note: Cluster 1 and Cluster 3 were interpreted as higher- and lower-proficiency groups, respectively; shorter completion time is better.
